publication_status: Official ACM policy explanation; badge version 1.1 effective after 2020-05-15
supported_claim: Results Reproduced: different team using authors' artifacts; Results Replicated: different team using independently developed artifacts.
applicability_caveat: Terminology changed in 2020. Paper II reuses inputs, so describe independently developed implementation precisely rather than asserting every artifact is independent.

publication_status: arXiv preprint; v2 revised 2026-06-22; separate peer-reviewed venue not verified
supported_claim: 270 tasks based on 90 papers across computer science, social science and medicine; uses provided code and data.
applicability_caveat: Computational artifact reproducibility, not independent implementation; curated CodeOcean artifacts are not the EPJ sampling frame.

supported_claim: FAIR principles: persistent identifiers, rich provenance metadata, versioning and licence information are required for findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable data.
applicability_caveat: FAIR addresses machine-actionable metadata and access conditions; it does not by itself guarantee that a specific historical input state used in a publication remains identifiable.

supported_claim: Data citation should use persistent identifiers and be specific enough to identify the exact data supporting a claim, including versions.
applicability_caveat: Declaration of principles, not an empirical evaluation; specificity/verifiability are stated goals.

supported_claim: Primary abstract states reproducibility terminology is nonstandard and unsettled across sciences.
applicability_caveat: Detailed methods/results/inferential taxonomy is mentioned in NASEM chapter 3; publisher full text unavailable here, so do not attribute a detailed verbatim definition on this audit alone.

supported_claim: Conceptual framework for dataset versioning: the same dataset name or identifier can refer to different revisions, releases and granularities; recommends explicit version identification.
applicability_caveat: Principles paper; supports the same-identifier ≠ same-version distinction conceptually.

supported_claim: Conclusion 3-1 defines reproducibility as consistent results using same input data/computational steps/methods/code; replicability requires studies obtaining their own data.
applicability_caveat: Independent reimplementation on reused data must not be described as a new-data replication under this convention. Its discussion of ACM reflects older terminology; use current ACM policy separately.

publication_status: Published ICLR 2026; arXiv first posted 2025, v5 2026
supported_claim: PaperCoder generates operational repositories through planning, analysis and code generation; assessed using model/human judgments and author repositories as ground truth when available.
applicability_caveat: Repository fidelity and execution/target reproduction must remain separate; evaluator access to reference code is not evidence that generation agents receive it.

supported_claim: 20 ICML 2024 papers; original authors' code and other online replications prohibited; paper plus author-clarification addendum; 8,316 rubric tasks.
applicability_caveat: Direct precedent. Author clarifications weaken a publication-only comparison; 21.0% is an average graded replication score, not a proportion of fully reconstructed papers; Code-Dev is a different endpoint.

supported_claim: Publisher abstract describes commercial software/version-access study sampling 10,000 articles across seven fields.
applicability_caveat: Does not measure independent reconstruction. Parent reports 10,000 rows but 9,935 unique PMIDs, not independently checked in this audit. Author-name indexing discrepancy also applies.

supported_claim: Argues that data provenance (derivation history from raw to analytical data) is required for reproducibility and reuse.
applicability_caveat: Perspective article; provenance capture tooling is not assessed in Paper II.

publication_status: Conference paper, 2013 IEEE International Conference on Big Data
supported_claim: Model for citing query results against dynamic databases using timestamped versioning and query persistence.
applicability_caveat: Reference implementation; not evidence about biomedical repositories in the Paper II corpus.

publication_status: Journal article, Harvard Data Science Review 3(4)
supported_claim: Describes adoption of the RDA dynamic-data citation recommendations across repositories and the role of versioning, timestamps and query persistence in re-identifying data subsets.
applicability_caveat: Focuses on repository-side infrastructure; independent third parties depend on repositories having implemented it.

publication_status: Research Data Alliance recommendation document (DataCite DOI)
supported_claim: Evolving/dynamic data require versioned, timestamped data stores, persistently identified queries, and query/result hashes so that a previously used data state can be re-identified and re-retrieved.
applicability_caveat: Recommendations for repositories; adoption is uneven and the recommendation does not report how often historical states are lost.

publication_status: arXiv preprint v2, 2025-11-23; separate peer-reviewed venue not verified
supported_claim: v2: 20 astrophysics papers and 111 expert-written tasks; masked manuscripts, supplied data/execution metadata and author collaboration. v1 explicitly prohibits original code.
applicability_caveat: v1 had 19 papers/107 tasks; use version-specific counts. v2 fetched text does not retain v1's explicit original-code prohibition sentence. Selected reproducible papers and some author-provided private inputs differ from a public-input population audit. Avoid abstract's under-20% shorthand: v2 Table 2 includes 0.22.

supported_claim: Recommends recording exact versions of external programs and archiving exact versions of all data and intermediate results.
applicability_caveat: Guidance; does not address legal limits on redistributing third-party data.

publication_status: Published ICLR 2025; first arXiv posting 2024; v3 2025
supported_claim: 102 tasks from 44 publications in four disciplines; agents produce standalone Python programs; expert-provided knowledge and evaluation data support the tasks.
applicability_caveat: Cross-disciplinary agent evaluation predates Paper II; curated task instructions are not unassisted reconstruction of an entire publication.

supported_claim: Recommends that data, code and workflow details, including software versions and persistent links, be made available with publication.
applicability_caveat: Policy recommendation; software-version drift is the EPJ antecedent's concern, dataset-version drift is treated here as analogous but distinct.

publication_status: Journal article, Computing in Science & Engineering 22(2)
supported_claim: Intrinsic, content-based cryptographic identifiers verify byte-level identity of an archived artifact independently of its location.
applicability_caveat: Concerns source code; a content hash verifies bytes that are available but cannot recover bytes that are no longer archived.

publication_status: Published Comment, Stem Cell Reviews and Reports, 2026-09-10
supported_claim: Publisher verifies title about environmental confounding in clonal systems and identifies a Comment, with retrospective GEO metadata noted in Data Availability.
applicability_caveat: Full article inaccessible in subscription preview; operational-system analogy is proposed interpretation, not a verified quantitative causal finding. Publisher/Crossref index given=Onishi, family=Tatsuki, differing from requested Onishi T.

supported_claim: Choice of genome annotation resource affects RNA-seq read mapping and gene quantification results.
applicability_caveat: Compares annotation sources, not release-to-release drift within one source; supports that the identity of an external reference resource can matter, not how often it matters in this corpus.
